recipes.name: Easy Southern Peach Cobbler
ingredients_raw: 1 (29 ounce) can sliced canned peaches, drained

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Grease a 9x9-inch baking dish.
Combine flour, brown sugar, white sugar, baking powder, salt, and vanilla in a large bowl. Pour milk into dry ingredients, and then stir in melted butter. Mix thoroughly.
Pour mixture into prepared baking pan. Arrange peaches on top and sprinkle with cinnamon. Bake in preheated oven until golden brown, about 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Southern Peach Cobbler
raw_recipe.description: This Southern peach cobbler recipe is easy to make with canned or fresh peaches, brown sugar, and vanilla for a great tasting summer dessert.

review.reviewBody:
I know a lot of people prefer a cobbler with a flaky crust, and if that is you try another recipe. I, on the other hand, love a thicker, cake-like crust. This crust reminds me of a good bread pudding, the edges have just a little crunch and the center is soft and custard like. If that is the kind of cobbler you preffer, then this is the best recipe.

I did make a couple of changes. I added a 1/4 cup more flour and milk to make more crust, and I used a smaller/deeper baking dish. I had to adjust the cooking time/temp a little for best results. 350-375 for 30 minutes then bump the temp to 400 for 10 minutes. Be sure to keep an eye on it in the last 10 minutes since. Everything was set perfectly for me at the 10 minute mark, but we all know there are a great number of factors that affect cook time.

Anyways, I'll be playing with this recipe some more, so if I come up with some bit thing that makes a significant change, I might be back.

This is a GREAT, easy, and delicious cobbler!! I used 5 fresh Palisades, Colorado peaches, which I had gotten in a large box from The Shriners, and these peaches were stunningly delicious! I used butter instead of marjarine, which I haven't used, or even purchased, in 30 years! I also used a little less white sugar, and mixed some large cut turbinado sugar with the cinnamon, and sprinkled the mix over the top as last step before baking. The whole pan is already gone!! It never had a chance!! I will make this over, and over!! It is almost too good warm, with vanilla bean ice cream on top!

Love this!!!! I made a few changes like other reviewers suggested. I doubled it and used a 9x13 baking dish. Instead of doubling the milk I used 3/4 cups of the syrup drained off the peaches and 3/4 cup of whole milk. I also mixed in cinnamon with the batter mixture. I think that he gave the crust a little extra special flavor. I was a little unsure of using the syrup from the Futures because I was afraid of how the crust would set up. But it set up perfect and it's very spongy when you press on it. I totally recommend using half milk and half syrup. It took about 40 minutes to bake on 400° in my oven

Saved the juice from the peaches to add to the batter if needed. Added cinnamon and nutmeg to batter. Stirred peaches up in bowl with cinnamon, nutmeg, brown sugar before placing on top. Doubled the recipe-- had to cook for over an hour in order for it to set. Cover top with foil to keep from burning. Very good!

I will definately make this again. Instead of putting the peaches on top, I sprinkled them with cinnamon and put them on the bottom. I took 1/4 cup of brown sugar and mixed it with 1/4 cup of the drained peach juice. I added 1/4 jar of marachino cheeries and poured it over the peaches. I also added an extra 1/4 cup of flour to the cake mix and 3 tablespoons of the peach juice. This made a moist cake with extra syrup to spoon over. My husband called it his cherry peach right side up cake.
Made this today. Used fresh unpealed peaches. Because I like a crispy crust, I substituted butter for milk. I baked it longer, about 45 mins. total. came out pretty good.

There are two kinds of cobbler: biscuit and crust. If you prefer crust, this recipe isn't for you. But if you prefer biscuit-style, you'll never need another cobbler recipe. This one is simple and delicious!

I used firmer, "just on the edge of becoming fully ripe" peaches so that they wouldn't get too soft and mushy during cooking. But that means I had to add 1 tsp sugar with the tsp of cinnamon when I coated them. 

Also, I put the peaches in the pan and poured the mix around them (rather than pouring the mix into the pan an putting the peaches on top). It worked out great.

My girl never used to like peach cobbler, but this is now one of her favorite desserts. Thanks for sharing.

Absolutely delicious!! My family couldn't get enough!!! The only change I made was to use butter because we don't use margarine and self rising flour. Remember to eliminate the baking powder/soda if using self rising flour. This definitely is a keeper!!!!

Never made this before. Followed the recipe and 2 recommendations; for adding 1/4 cup flour and milk, plus lowering the temperature to 350-375 for 30 minutes and 400 for the last 10. It turned out fantastic and was a hit with everyone! Thank you.

This cobbler is so easy to make and has a great taste. I used fresh peaches instead of canned. I only had four large peaches, so I halved the recipe and it turned out very good. I used a smaller baking dish and baked it for a shorter period of time. When I make it again I will still use fresh peaches but will open a can of peaches and use the peach juice in the recipe. I think it will add to the peachy flavor of the cobbler. I had a jar of cinnamon/sugar in the cupboard and sprinkled that on top of the cobbler before baking. Enjoyed very much and will definitely make again. Also will try this recipe with different fruits.

Karen, Thank you! This is exactly what grandma made back in the 1950s and '60s: the batter goes on the bottom, the fruit on top and while cooking they switch places and the flavors meld along the way. The top browned perfectly and there's plenty of juice. My stove took 35 minutes at 400F. Being spring my 9x9 Pyrex seems to have found its way into the garden shed where it seems to be sprouting a crop of coleus (must speak to my significant other about that) so your recipe perfectly filled a 7 1/2 x 11 Pyrex. Flavor is spot on. MANY THANKS!
Made the recipe as is. It never completely browned. The flavor was good, but it was too dry for my liking.

The flavor was good on this, but it didn't turn out right as the top and edges were getting dark, but the entire middle was foamy and raw looking. The peaches didn't cook long enough and were still fairly firm and didn't break down and become super soft like cooked peach pie or cobbler usually does. I scooped out the edges and served what was set.
So good. I cheated and used canned peaches. Because that's actually all I had available. I reserved the juice the peaches were in and cooked its stove top with a little sugar to make a glaze.
This didn’t work for me. After 30 minutes it was burnt on the edges and the middle was foamy and raw.
Great recipe. I needed to keep in the oven for more than 30 minutes.
We love this cake like cobbler! Do you think it would work with berries?
I made this recipe with my daughter we loved it and so did the family! Thank you!
I added about a third cup chopped pecans. It was delicious!
Haven’t tasted it yet but seems to have turned out pretty good
